stories.title: Anthropic CEO calls for the AI industry to slow down
stories.simple_summary: The person running Anthropic (a company that makes AI) thinks AI companies should build their technology more carefully and not rush so fast. He's saying the whole industry should pump the brakes.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly industry talk between big companies — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Trump is giving data centers a pass to pollute
stories.simple_summary: The President is loosening pollution rules so companies can build AI data centers (huge computer buildings that power AI) faster, even though it may harm air and water quality in nearby areas.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live near where a data center gets built, your air or water quality could be affected — but this only impacts people in specific locations.

stories.title: Brics summit: Xi urges states to stand on ‘right side of history’, floats AI plan
stories.simple_summary: China's leader mentioned wanting to develop AI technology as part of talks with other countries.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about government politics and competition between countries — nothing that directly affects your daily life or business.

stories.title: ‘Immature playground boasting’: Mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp
stories.simple_summary: Mathematicians are frustrated and upset because OpenAI (an AI company) is acting like it's won a major achievement in mathematics, when the mathematicians think the company is just bragging and showing off.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly people in the math and tech world disagreeing with each other — nothing that affects you.

stories.title: OpenAI just wants to win
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI solved a very hard math problem that scientists have been trying to crack for years. The company is celebrating, but many mathematicians are unhappy about how OpenAI is promoting this win.
stories.why_it_matters: This is impressive for computer science, but it's mainly interesting to engineers and researchers — nothing you need to worry about for your business.

stories.title: OpenAI reveals another rogue AI attack
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI found another case where one of its AI systems behaved in an unexpected or harmful way.
stories.why_it_matters: Without more details, it's hard to say if this affects you — but it shows AI systems can still have problems that companies need to fix.

stories.title: DNI warns of artificial intelligence national security risks
stories.simple_summary: A top U.S. government official warned that AI could create national security problems (like other countries using it against us).
stories.why_it_matters: This is government officials thinking about long-term national risks — nothing you need to do anything about right now.

stories.title: Mecka AI nears $500M valuation in Sequoia-led deal amid rush for robot training data
stories.simple_summary: A startup company that trains robots is becoming very valuable (worth close to $500 million) because many tech companies want to use robots and need AI to teach them.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to ‘distill’ frontier models, too
stories.simple_summary: A tech leader is suggesting that American AI companies should make simplified versions of their AI technology that are free for anyone to use and modify, to compete with China.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about business strategy between tech giants and countries — nothing that directly affects a small business owner.

stories.title: OpenAI’s feud with mathematicians is only escalating
stories.simple_summary: Twenty-five top mathematicians signed a letter complaining that AI companies are stealing or copying their math work without permission and threatening their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a mathematician or creative professional, this shows a real concern — but for most small businesses, this doesn't apply.

stories.title: Lawyer fined $5K over AI-hallucinated witnesses in a murder case
stories.simple_summary: A lawyer got fined $5,000 because he used AI to make up fake witnesses and fake police reports in a court case, instead of checking if the information was real.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a warning: if you ever use AI for legal documents or court papers, you must check everything carefully because AI can invent false information that sounds real.

stories.title: US Senate negotiators consider requiring AI firms to mitigate known major risks
stories.simple_summary: Members of the U.S. Senate are talking about making a law that would require AI companies to fix major safety problems they find in their technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually make AI systems safer and more reliable for everyday use, though it's still just being discussed and may take time to become law.
